cases.title: Conflicting Geography
cases.notes: Liam wants to stay within a 3-hour drive of family in Chicago, but his mother is demanding warm coastal weather year-round in California or Florida. Looking for business or engineering programs. Unweighted GPA 3.7, ACT 29. Needs an urban or suburban setting with strong internship access.
cases.why_hard: The student and family have stated geographic requirements that are physically mutually exclusive.

cases.title: High Stats with Critical Need-Based Aid
cases.notes: Maya has a 4.0 UW GPA and 1560 SAT with stellar robotics ECs, aiming for engineering. However, family expected contribution is $0 and she cannot take on loans, requiring 100% demonstrated need met or heavy merit guarantees while keeping academic rigor high.
cases.why_hard: High academic stats require balancing top-tier selectivity with strict, unyielding financial need constraints.

cases.title: Test-Optional with Missing Scores
cases.notes: Julian has a 3.85 GPA with rigorous AP coursework in AP Bio and AP Env Sci, targeting biology or environmental_science. He has no SAT or ACT scores due to repeated test center cancellations and needs schools where test-optional policies carry zero penalty for institutional aid.
cases.why_hard: The system must evaluate academic fit and aid eligibility without standardized test benchmarks.

cases.title: Program Not in Tool Directory
cases.notes: Sienna is set on studying Game Development and Sound Architecture with a complete digital portfolio. GPA 3.5, SAT 1280. She is unsure whether to select art, design, or computer_science in system drop-downs to capture her target major.
cases.why_hard: The student's desired field does not map directly to the tool's pre-defined list of supported majors.

cases.title: Wide Open and Hedging Majors
cases.notes: Ethan is torn between nursing, business, and art. GPA 3.4, ACT 24. Wants a mid-sized university where he can easily switch majors or complete pre-requisites without getting locked out by capped or direct-entry program rules.
cases.why_hard: The majors spanned have radically different admissions thresholds, college structures, and internal transfer restrictions.

cases.title: Extremely Sparse Notes
cases.notes: Chloe. GPA around 3.2. Wants agriculture or marine_biology. East Coast preferred. Budget around $35k total per year.
cases.why_hard: Minimal details force the tool to make broad assumptions without clear context on test scores, preferences, or profile strength.

cases.title: Overconstrained Criteria
cases.notes: Noah insists on direct-entry nursing in downtown Boston for under $15,000 total net price per year, but currently holds a 2.7 GPA and 980 SAT. He refuses community college pathways or non-urban options.
cases.why_hard: The combination of low academic scores, hyper-specific geography, competitive major, and low budget yields zero mathematical matches.

cases.title: Homeschool Without Standard GPA
cases.notes: Freya has been homeschooled through high school without official letter grades or a GPA, but submitted a project narrative and a 1420 SAT. She wants computer_science or law pathways at institutions comfortable evaluating narrative transcript portfolios.
cases.why_hard: The lack of a traditional GPA breaks standard admissibility filter algorithms.

cases.title: High Stats and Extremely Risk-Averse
cases.notes: Caleb holds a 3.98 UW GPA and 1540 SAT in heavy STEM coursework. Interested in engineering. He feels intense anxiety around rejection and refuses to apply to hyper-selective schools, wanting a list dominated by highly predictable options with top honors colleges and auto-merit.
cases.why_hard: The student's high profile suggests highly selective reach options, but emotional preferences require filtering for high-admit options with strong honors features.

cases.title: Parental Brand Pressure vs. Low Stats
cases.notes: Zara's parents demand she only apply to nationally recognizable, household-name universities for business or law. However, Zara has an unweighted GPA of 2.9, SAT of 1050, and minimal extracurricular involvement.
cases.why_hard: Unrealistic parental demands for prestige directly contradict the student's actual academic metrics.
